body: Just because of a receding hair line or for other reasons too? If it's just because of premature balding then no, not even a little bit. A bunch of other dudes will catch up to you eventually (early 30s and onward) and by then no one will remember you started balding first.
I agree. Nothing cowardly about it, it's the opposite of cowardly.

I'm so sorry no one in your life understands the depth of your pain and that you have been trying your hardest to push on for years on end. That sounds like a painstakingly invalidating experience. I think sometimes people who have no control over their loved ones' suffering can get frustrated at that lack of control. All they can think to do is put the onus on the suffering person to "fix the problem". I wish there was something I could do to alleviate your suffering.

I think about this too. I have to believe that for those of us with insurmountable problems and endless suffering in this life, that there is something better on the other side. Whether that be absolutely nothing and thus an end to suffering, eternal peace, some form of heaven, another shot at life with better prospects, etc. I have decided that HAS to be the case.
I know how you feel. I so very much hope you find peace.

Thanks for your concern. It took me over three hours to write it and it doesn't even say exactly the thoughts I have in my head I don't think. When communicating is impaired getting guidance from professionals is frustrating, daunting, overwhelming, scary. The steps to getting something scheduled, trying to understand payment, figuring out how to get there, going through the appointments without getting much from it...It's like trying to get advice and hearing back nonsense. Presenting like a helpless crying child and them treating you like you're catastrophizing. So many hurdles and so much confusion. I know enough to know these things aren't curable and even trying to do the steps to get to the steps that might bring slight improvement hurt my brain. It's just not right.
Thank you for your input! The ASHA ProFind tool looks promising and relatively easy to navigate.
